text: The cosmological constant can be added to the field equations as G_μν + Λ g_μν = 8πG T_μν/c⁴. Why is this addition consistent with local energy-momentum conservation ∇_μ T^μν = 0?
choices: Because metric compatibility gives ∇_μ g^μν = 0, so the Λ g_μν term is automatically divergence-free, exactly like G_μν
Because Λ is chosen small enough that its divergence is negligible in practice
Because g_μν is antisymmetric, so Λ g_μν drops out of the conservation law
Because the cosmological constant only affects the trace of the equations, not their divergence
explanation: Metric compatibility of the Levi-Civita connection means ∇_μ g^μν = 0, so Λ g_μν is identically divergence-free, just as G_μν is divergence-free by the contracted Bianchi identity. Taking the covariant divergence of both sides therefore still yields ∇_μ T^μν = 0. The consistency is exact, not approximate; g_μν is symmetric, not antisymmetric; and this is why Lovelock's theorem admits precisely the combination α G_μν + Λ g_μν.
